Starts or restarts the descent: waits for the raster to wrap, blanks the screen, resets the stack, stops the music and the sound effects, clears zero page $80-$FF and the workspace $0600-$07FF, selects VIC-II bank 3 ($C000, set_vic_bank with A=0), loads 47 VIC-II registers from $83D3, points the raster call at level_raster ($80D1) and takes over the sprites ($045A, $0463).

The ring speed $93 comes from speed_table by the PAL/NTSC flag $0200: $50 on PAL, $60 on NTSC. Then the script starts at step 0 ($A7 = $FF, so the first tick moves it to 0) with a delay of one, the HUD's flicker colours $A4/$A5 are 9, and the four rings start at $5400 across, $8500 down.

Copies the colour map from $E000-$E3FF to colour RAM, points sprite 2 at frame $C0 (the compliance indicator), turns on the raster interrupt and waits for ever: from here everything runs in the interrupt.
The level's idle loop.
The raster call, once a frame. Runs level_frame (the trainer's skip key, the clock, the music and the effects), then, unless paused or idle, the script (script_tick).

The screen shake: while $9D is non-zero, every $9E+1 frames a new random x offset ($96) and y offset ($97) are drawn, each ANDed with $9D. The offsets go into the fine-scroll bits of $D016 and $D011, so the whole screen jumps. With $9D at zero the offsets are 0 and 3, the screen at rest.
The BPL's offset byte, $10, doubles as a mask: the BIT at $8188 tests the sprite-enable bits against it.
While the ending formation flies ($A6 set), the rest of the frame is skipped: the sky raster loop takes over.
Sprites 0 and 1 (the landing beacons) blink between dark grey and white with bit 1 of the clock $0209.
The background colours $D021 and $D022 flicker: each frame picks $A1 or $A2 at random (the colours set by the flicker steps), and the same random bit picks $A4 or $A5 as the HUD colour at $AD31.
Named by the trainer of another stage; here part of the flicker.
The STA's operand, $D021; named by another stage's trainer.
The operand's high byte.
Moves the raster loop's colour table pointer (the LDY operand at $8740) back by the y shake, so the HUD's colour bands shake with the screen.
With none of the ring sprites 3-7 on and the pipe of rings off ($9A), skips the rings and goes to the deviation check.
Steers (steer), then adds the speed $93 to the fraction $92. Each carry moves the depth step $94 (0-7) on by one; when it wraps to 0 the rings move one place nearer (new_ring).
Stores the depth step.

A new ring appears. The sprite-enable bits for 3-7 shift down by one: a ring leaving sprite 5 turns on sprites 3 and 4 together (the nearest ring), and sprite 7 gets a new far ring only while the pipe is on ($9A bit 7). The ring count $95 goes on; after 256 rings one tick is added to the script's countdown.
The ring colours move down with the rings (sprite 5's to 3 and 4, 6's to 5, 7's to 6), and the new ring in sprite 7 is light blue or yellow, alternately, from $847A.
The positions move down too: ring 2 to 3, 1 to 2, 0 to 1. The four rings' x are $80-$83 (fraction) and $84-$87, their y $88-$8B and $8C-$8F, ring 0 the farthest.
The new ring 0 is the old one moved by the path: the ring count $95 picks a step across from path_x ($944C) and a step down from path_y ($954C). The path is the course the player has to steer.
Turbulence: while $9B is set, the shake offsets also push the rings, by -1, 0 or +1 from jolt_table, doubled for each nearer ring, so rough air throws the course about.

Places the three far rings: sprite 5 is ring 2, sprite 6 ring 1, sprite 7 ring 0. Each ring's position is halved into screen pixels, offset (by 6 and 10 for ring 2) and moved by the shake; the ninth x bits collect in $98.

The nearest ring, ring 3, is drawn by sprites 3 and 4 down the whole screen, redrawn line by line by the raster loop. Its x goes into the loop's ADC operands at $877D and $87A7 and its ninth bit into $8783 and $87AD; its top line $90/$91 is its y less the half height for the depth step (near_ring_half).
Writes the ninth x bits of sprites 5-7, then the frames for the depth step: sprite 7 from $8402, 6 from $840A, 5 from $8412, 3 and 4 from $841A, so each ring grows as it comes nearer.

Points the raster loop at the near ring's tables for this depth step, each less the ring's top line: x of sprite 3 ($8422) into $8779, its ninth bit ($8432) into $8780, x of sprite 4 ($8442) into $87A3, its ninth bit ($8452) into $87AA, and the visibility table ($8462) into $8760.

How far the nearest ring is from the centre of the screen ($54 across, $84 down): with a the larger and b the smaller distance, 2a+b. At $50 or more the drop-ship has strayed: the distance is held in $A0, and the script jumps to step $35, so the next tick runs step $36, the crash. The trainer turns this off by writing JMP $83AA at $839C.
The BNE the trainer overwrites with JMP $83AA, so the crash is never set off.
Part of the BNE and STA the trainer overwrites.
Stores the distance that set off the crash.
The compliance indicator, sprite 2, drops by the distance: its y is $4D plus the distance (capped at $78) plus the shake, its x 9 plus the shake.

The raster call never returns. It resets the stack, turns interrupts back on and spins in a raster loop until the next frame's interrupt starts the call again: the pipe loop ($873C), or the sky loop ($87CC) once the ending formation flies.
The ring speed by the PAL/NTSC flag $0200: $60 for NTSC ($0200 = $FF, read at $83C9), $50 for PAL.
The turbulence push for a shake offset 0-7: +1, +1, 0, 0, 0, 0, -1, -1.

The frame for sprite 5 (ring 2) at each depth step, $BB-$BF.
The frame for sprites 3 and 4 (ring 3) at each depth step, $B6-$BA.

The new ring's colour, light blue ($0E) and yellow ($07) in turn.

The level is a script of 58 timed steps. $A8 counts down once per clock tick (when $020A, the frames to the next tick, is 1); at zero the step $A7 moves on by one. $A9 set makes the current step run every frame instead.
Runs step $A7: its delay from script_delay ($8702) into $A8, and its handler from script_lo ($8654) and script_hi ($868E) patched into the JMP at $84A5.
The handler's address, written by script_next: the snapshot holds $8618.
The high byte of the handler's address.
Nothing to do this frame.
Step $2B: the landing beacons, sprites 0 and 1, appear side by side at ($A8, $98) and ($AC, $98) in frame $C1, with their speeds $AA/$AB cleared.

Step $2D, every frame: every eighth frame the music's volume drops by one, and the beacons fly apart and down, faster each frame (the speed $AA/$AB grows by 2), as the drop-ship comes in over them. Their frame changes from $C1 to $C3 as they speed up; when sprite 0 is off the left of the screen the script goes on.
The STA's operand, $D002; named by another stage's trainer.

Step $29, every frame until the last ring sprite (3-7) has passed: then the script goes on.

Lights the HUD: its colour at $AD30 becomes light green ($0D), the compliance indicator (sprite 2) comes on, and hud_colours colours the cockpit's gauges.

The joystick steers the drop-ship. First the velocity across ($BB/$BC) and down ($BD/$BE) are pulled towards zero by the drag at $8E04-$8E0B (by $0200, PAL or NTSC); then the joystick's directions ($0222) pick an acceleration from $8E14/$8E34 and $8E54/$8E74.
The speed is capped at $8E0C across and $8E0E down, either way (negate_velocity flips a negative speed and back).
Moves the rings: the velocity is added to ring 3, then grows by half for each farther ring, so the far rings slide more than the near ones and the pipe bends as the ship turns.
Negates the 16-bit value in $B9/$BA and sets X to $FF to say so.

Unpacks the file just loaded, reading its bytes through get_byte ($C403). First it builds three tables of 52 entries (bit counts at $C2E6, base low at $C31A, base high at $C34E), then copies literal bytes and back-references downwards from the end address in $FE/$FF. The tables' layout is that of the Exomizer decruncher, so it is probably the cracker's, not Activision's.
Reads X bits from the stream into A (low) and $FC (high), refilling the bit buffer $FD from get_byte.

Sends the drive the pair 0, 2, then releases the lines. The drive's side of the protocol is not in memory, so what the pair means is unknown; it is sent when a file is not found and at a file's end.

Keeps the name's address in the LDA at $C43D, then asks the drive for track 0, sector 1, which the drive's own code must take as the directory (the entries compared are directory entries), and reads it, sector by sector, comparing each file's name with the wanted one: * ends the match and ? matches any character. A file whose type is PRG ($82, closed) and whose name matches opens at its first track and sector.
Checks the entry's file type.
The name's address, written by find_file.
The high byte of the name's address.
The name's length, written by find_file into this CPY's operand: the compare stops after that many characters.
Next directory entry (32 bytes each), then the next directory sector.
Not found: releases the drive and returns with the carry set.
Found: reads the file's first sector.
Returns with the carry clear (found) or set (a read error), and starts at the sector's first byte.
Releases the serial lines (CIA 2 port A bits 3-5 back to inputs).
Takes the serial lines for the fast transfer.
The body of get_byte: hands out the next byte of the sector buffer at $C602; when the sector is used up, follows its link to the next sector and fetches it. A link track of 0 ends the file.

Sends X and Y (track and sector) to the drive two bits at a time over the clock and data lines.
Sends one byte, two bits at a time.
